about: Research sheet for the Oregon county edition. Every contact below was read on the date in reviewed_on from the page named beside it; scripts/make_county_state.py turns it into the edition files.
name: Oregon
phones_sentence: County veterans office phones, addresses and hours come from the Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs county pages. Many offices work by appointment; call before you go.

offices.source_title: Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs: County Services Directory
offices.note: County veteran service officers are trained and certified by the Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs and help with VA claims, pension, survivor benefits and appeals at no charge. The department’s line, 800-692-9666, can also help.
offices.selection: Office address, phones and hours as printed on the county’s page in the department’s directory; officers’ names, email addresses and fax numbers omitted. Counties with more than one office list the others.

programs.name: Oregon veterans: county veteran service officers for claims help
programs.organization: County veteran services offices and the Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs
programs.description: Free help with VA claims, appeals, pension and survivor benefits from county veteran service officers, who are trained and certified by the Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs. Every county has an office.
programs.next_step: Choose your county for its office, or call the Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs at 800-692-9666 (503-373-2085).
constraints: Many offices work by appointment and some are open only certain days; call before you go.

sources.scope: Links to the 36 county pages; read in full.

sources.scope: Department contact 800-692-9666 or 503-373-2085 and the Marion County office; read in full.

programs.name: Aging and Disability Resource Connection of Oregon
programs.organization: Oregon Department of Human Services, Aging and People with Disabilities
programs.description: Oregon’s statewide aging and disability line. Trained staff talk through your situation and connect you to the local Area Agency on Aging for meals, in-home help, caregiver support and long-term care options. Military service is not required.
programs.next_step: Call 855-673-2372 (855-ORE-ADRC), or choose a county above for its Area Agency on Aging.
constraints: Each program has its own eligibility and waitlist.
Give your county so the call reaches the right agency.

sources.title: Oregon Department of Human Services: Aging and disability contacts

programs.name: Medicare counseling (SHIBA) for Oregon
programs.organization: Oregon Department of Human Services, Senior Health Insurance Benefits Assistance (SHIBA)
programs.description: Free Medicare counseling from SHIBA’s certified volunteer counselors: plan choices, enrollment, costs and help paying for Medicare.
programs.next_step: Call SHIBA at 800-722-4134. For Medicare itself, call 800-MEDICARE (800-633-4227).
constraints: Have your Medicare card and drug list ready.

sources.title: Oregon SHIBA: Get help
sources.scope: Statewide phone 800-722-4134 and counseling sites; search excerpt.

programs.name: Oregon Long-Term Care Ombudsman and adult abuse reporting
programs.organization: Oregon Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman
programs.description: Independent advocacy for residents of nursing homes, assisted living, residential care and adult foster homes.
programs.next_step: Call the ombudsman at 800-522-2602 (503-378-6533). To report suspected abuse, neglect or financial exploitation of an older adult or an adult with a disability, call the Oregon SAFEline at 855-503-SAFE (855-503-7233), 24 hours a day. In an emergency, call 911.
constraints: The ombudsman acts with the resident’s permission and is not a licensing agency.

sources.title: Oregon Blue Book: Office of the Long-Term Care Ombudsman
Oregon Department of Human Services: How to report abuse or neglect
sources.scope: Call 855-503-SAFE (7233) about an older person or vulnerable adult; open 24 hours a day; search excerpt.

programs.name: Free legal help for Oregon veterans and older adults
programs.organization: Legal Aid Services of Oregon and Oregon Law Center; Oregon State Bar
programs.description: Oregon’s legal aid programs run a statewide Public Benefits Hotline for low-income Oregonians with problems getting or keeping benefits. Area Agencies on Aging fund some legal help for people 60 and older. The Oregon State Bar’s Military Assistance Panel connects deployed service members and their families with volunteer lawyers.
programs.next_step: Call the Public Benefits Hotline at 800-520-5292 (Monday and Thursday 1–4 p.m.; Tuesday and Wednesday 9 a.m.–noon). Ask your Area Agency on Aging about senior legal help. For the Military Assistance Panel or a lawyer referral, call the Oregon State Bar at 503-684-3763 or 800-452-7636.
constraints: Legal aid screens by income and case type.
The Military Assistance Panel is for service members around deployment and their families.

programs.description: Oregon veterans are served mainly by the VA Portland Health Care System (Portland VA Medical Center, 3710 SW U.S. Veterans Hospital Road, 503-220-8262 or 800-949-1004), the Roseburg VA Health Care System (913 NW Garden Valley Boulevard, Roseburg, 541-440-1000) and the VA Southern Oregon Rehabilitation Center and Clinics in White City (541-826-2111), with clinics across the state.
programs.next_step: Use VA’s facility locator with your ZIP code to find the closest clinic. Not enrolled yet? Ask your county veteran service officer for help applying.
constraints: Which system serves you depends on where you live; VA’s locator shows the right clinic.

coverage_scope: Referral edition. All 36 counties have a county veterans service office, a matched Area Agency on Aging and the statewide long-term care ombudsman; 25 counties are served by a Center for Independent Living.
coverage_note: County veterans offices come from the Oregon Department of Veterans’ Affairs county pages. Area Agencies on Aging and their counties come from the Department of Human Services’ June 2026 overview, with each agency’s phone from its own or a state page. Centers for Independent Living come from the state’s 2024 directory; 11 counties have no center.
